text:
viv: weird one from a partner trying to resume a stalled stream. they did a last-event-id resume and we got a late fragment that replays a previously-received chunk, then the client concatenated and json.parse failed. repro on Chrome + service-worker network proxy. anyone seen resume + late-fragment dupes?

noah: that feels different from the pure post-[DONE] drops we've been doing. do you have the raw sequence?

viv: yep, tcp capture from their env below. note the repeated chunk id `c3` arriving twice with an intervening DONE marker on the first connection.

viv: ```
data: {"chunk_id":"c1","text":"hello"}
data: {"chunk_id":"c2","text":" world"}
data: [DONE]

-- reconnect with Last-Event-ID: c2 --
data: {"chunk_id":"c2","text":" world"}
data: {"chunk_id":"c3","text":"!"}
```

elena: aha. so the resume replayed a previous chunk (`c2`) and the client concatenated frames producing `{"chunk_id":"c2","text":" world"}{"chunk_id":"c3","text":"!"}` which our naive parser tried to JSON.parse as one blob and blew up.

noah: two possible fixes: 1) make server include a monotonic sequence header so clients can reassemble safely, 2) client-side robust reassembly that treats consecutive data lines as independent objects and parses per-line, or 3) client dedupe by `chunk_id` when resuming.

viv: I pushed a local patch that changes the JS sample reassembler to parse per-line (split on `\n`) and then ignore duplicates by keeping a small LRU of recent `chunk_id`s. prevents this crash and preserves delivered content.

elena: preserving content is nice; dropping post-DONE fragments loses ambiguous late tokens. dedupe seems better UX if chunk_ids are present. do we guarantee chunk_id in all models/servers?

noah: currently we don't mandate `chunk_id` metadata in frames to keep server simple. but it is being emitted by a few model backends we onboarded. adding it as optional but common practice might be okay. alternatively, clients can parse-per-line and then fallback to post-DONE drop if no ids are present.

viv: implemented fallback: parse-per-line always; if a line has `chunk_id` do dedupe; otherwise, drop lines that arrive after a final marker or are exact text duplicates in the last N lines. avoids panics without requiring server changes.

sdk-bot: Created ticket SDK-3418 - "Streaming reassembly: per-line parsing + optional chunk_id dedupe across SDKs" (reporter: viv)

elena: nice. cross-SDK parity request: JS/py/go should implement line-wise reassembly + optional dedupe LRU keyed by `chunk_id` (opt-in via config). default to enabled for onboarding sampleapp. also add a telemetry metric `stream.duplicate_chunk_dropped`.

noah: infra note: we should still audit proxies/service-workers that can replay frames during resume; opened INFRA-1307 to check proxy resume semantics and Last-Event-ID handling. infra-bot: please link when ready.

infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-1307 - "Audit proxies and service-worker caches for SSE resume replay behavior"

viv: i'll open PRs: small JS sampleapp patch + change in the JS SDK reassembler and tests. then mirror in python/go once we agree on the LRU size default (100 recent ids?).

elena: LRU=128 seems fine. make it configurable. include a unit test that simulates: initial connection yields c1,c2,[DONE], then resume replays c2,c3 and ensure parser emits c1,c2,c3 exactly once in order.

noah: add a short README note in sampleapp: "If you use Last-Event-ID resume with intermediaries, clients perform per-line parsing and optional dedupe by chunk_id to avoid duplicate tokens."

viv: good plan. this keeps server surface minimal but avoids losing content for users. thanks team.
